name: SBFC Finance Ltd
title: SBFC Finance Ltd - 543959 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: SBFC Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27% YoY to INR 139 crore, with ROE at 15.04% and AUM up 27% YoY to INR 12,592 crore.
summary.overview: SBFC reported its 36th consecutive quarter of sequential AUM and profit growth, with AUM at INR 12,592 crore (up 6% QoQ, 27% YoY) and PAT of INR 139 crore (up 7% QoQ, 27% YoY). Credit cost eased to 1.37% from 1.44% and Opex fell to 4.07%, while spreads widened to 9.63%. Management said the gold-loan delinquency rise after the RBI circular was the main source of higher Stage 2 assets, and that the MSME book has stabilised rather than improved. Management kept its 5-7% quarterly AUM growth guidance and warned against treating 9.6% spreads as a new norm.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME AUM INR 9,669 crore (77% of AUM), up 18% YoY and 4.3% QoQ; on-book grew 20% and co-origination 10%. MSME disbursements INR 855 crore, up 6% QoQ, the third straight quarter of growth.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan AUM INR 2,906 crore (about 23% of AUM); added INR 275 crore in Q2, roughly INR 40 lakh net growth per branch per month across 236 gold branches. Management is deliberately cautious on volume and LTV expansion.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 5-7% per quarter going forward; management said MSME disbursements should grow in double digits second-half over second-half.
Opex expected to fall by a further 25 bps in FY27, with a further reduction over the next two quarters.
Spread guided around 9-9.25%, but management asked investors not to model 9.6% as the norm due to rising gold competition and likely pricing rationalisation.
Credit cost seen stabilising at around 1.37% or marginally lower unless El Nino or state waivers materially change the outlook; 1.45% in Q1 described as likely peak.
Capital sufficient to an AUM of about INR 20,000 crore before the next capital raise; ROE expansion expected as leverage rises.
PLR raised 25 bps in October 2026; management expects spreads to hold as variable-rate MSME assets reprice.
CARE and India Ratings revised outlook from stable to positive.
capex_capacity: Branch count 257 as of September 2026 (1 added in Q2, 6 in H1); 236 branches do gold loans.
Collection team about 850 including supervisors (about 700 front-end), up 150-200 in the period.
LCR at 194%; closing liquidity INR 1,782 crore in Q2 versus INR 1,864 crore in Q1.
AI voice ran the first full pre-due collection cycle in October: more than 4 lakh calls to 35,000 accounts, 84% reached, 53% paid, replacing roughly a 60-person team.
demand_pricing: Banks are moving to higher-ticket prime borrowers at single-digit pricing, leaving INR 10-25 lakh and INR 25+ lakh MSME segments with headroom for SBFC.
Sub-INR 7 lakh book is being run down and is no longer originated; it is under 6% of AUM per management.
Gold competition rising as large players open branches; gold yields range 18-21%, with management expecting roughly 23% and possibly 25%.
Co-origination rose to INR 112 crore from INR 78 crore in Q1.
Management expects MSME disbursements to stabilise and grow; Q2 was the highest disbursement level in the MSME business since listing per management.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan stress and how the industry is positioned, given larger players entering gold.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not chase high-volume gold growth, as it expects pricing to be compromised; it said gold yields are 18-21% and competition has risen in the last 1-1.5 months, with some large players opening 500-1,000 branches.

qa_highlights.question: Why slippages (GS2+GS3) rose QoQ, and whether the ARC sale was gold or MSME.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise in Stage 2 is entirely from gold loans after the RBI circular reset scheme design, as customers move from bullet to monthly interest payments. The ARC sale was a lower-ticket vintage LAP portfolio; no gold loans were sold.

qa_highlights.question: Gold price sensitivity and LTV risk.
qa_highlights.answer: LTV fell to 67% from about 70% last quarter (versus about 60s in June 2025). Auctions are triggered after 85-90% LTV and delinquency, with a 7-30 day window per management; out-of-money risk described as not significant.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of MSME disbursement pick-up.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the repositioning is done and restaffing is complete in most locations; it expects second-half over second-half disbursement growth of at least double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state 0+ DPD and credit cost.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 0+ rose from around 7% to above 9% and is now stabilising; it expects 0+ to hold in the 8-9.2% range, not return to 7%, and credit cost to stabilise near 1.37%.

qa_highlights.question: Whether 4.5% ROA can be sustained as guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROA has held above 4.5% for 7-8 quarters despite higher leverage; holding 4.6% over the long run will be difficult, but it should hold in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: Collection headcount and bandwidth.
qa_highlights.answer: About 700 front-end collectors and 850 including supervisors; average caseload of 40-45 per collector, varying from 25-30 in Assam to about 50 in South India.

risks_watch: Gold: competitive pricing pressure, possible yield compression, and a possible fall in gold prices (LTV fell to 67%; October saw a drop).
El Nino and drought: rainfall deficit concentrated in Karnataka and Maharashtra; state-level waivers could affect repayment behaviour.
Rising rates: 25 bps repo hike and cost of funds expected to rise; management expects spreads to hold, but pass-through of MCLR-linked debt is still to come.
Draft regulatory circular that management said may affect profitability.
Stage 2 and 0+ DPD trends, with 0+ above 9% versus about 7% historically; track whether they keep stabilising in Q3.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics and conservative in outlook: management stressed consistency and 'boring' results, repeatedly cautioned on gold and macro risk, and said asset quality has stabilised rather than improved. It was evasive on the precise gold-loan granularity an analyst asked for, promising to consider adding it to future presentations.
key_quotes: We are building SBFC to deliver consistent quarterly performance despite the noise.
Please do not pencil in 9.6% in your models as the new norm, since competitive intensity in gold is rising and some pricing rationalization is likely.
So to say that will it go below 7% will be a tall ask. We don't think it will reach there.
In our case, we've been able to hold on to more than 4.5% ROA for now more than 7 - 8 quarters despite increase in leverage.

adds.what: 1 new branch added in Q2 (257 branches as of Sep 2026, 6 added in H1); no further branch openings quantified

growth.why: Management held 5-7% quarterly AUM growth guidance (about 22-32% annualised) and 25 bps FY27 opex reduction, backed by MSME disbursements of INR 855 crore (third straight quarter of growth), 257 branches and banks retreating to higher-ticket segments, but no specific capacity or order-book numbers beyond that; reported PAT growth was 27% YoY.
